content:
david: Heads-up — noticed a few orgs hit sustained bursts and our smoothing rule is oscillating allocation. We should sync on options before we push the UX change tomorrow.
maya: can you paste an example trace / metric?
david: here’s a short window from yesterday: 
```
2026-02-14T15:03:10Z org=acme tokens=12000 rps=38 burst_tokens=32 smoothing_alloc=0.6
2026-02-14T15:03:20Z org=acme tokens=25000 rps=72 burst_tokens=120 smoothing_alloc=0.3
2026-02-14T15:03:30Z org=acme tokens=18000 rps=45 burst_tokens=48 smoothing_alloc=0.53
```
maya: thx — that looks like the allocator overreacts to short high-rps spikes. smoothing window is 30s right?
priya: current default is 30s with a decay alpha=0.2. Short spikes push the EWMA down then it takes a while to recover.
chris: are we sure this is an allocator bug vs telemetry lag? Could be late metrics from edge caches.
david: good call. I verified the gateway logs: we get bursts at the edge, central quota service sees them 2–3s later, but that alone doesn't explain the magnitude of the drop.
emma: quick question for product: do we prefer strict per-key fair share or softer per-org smoothing to avoid completely throttling small teams during neighbor noise?
sara: from billing perspective, strict per-key is easier, but it causes a lot of support tickets where customers complain about noisy neighbors stealing bursts.
priya: design options: 
1) Move burst enforcement to edge gateway (fast, lower central load) — risk: edges have partial view so fairness suffers.
2) Keep central enforcement + predictive smoothing (longer horizon + anomaly detection) — fairer but higher latency and complexity.
3) Hybrid: edge admits short bursts locally up to X tokens, central reconciles and retroactively throttles/credits.
chris: hybrid looks promising. We already have a small local token bucket per connection. Increase that to handle sub-5s spikes?
maya: hybrid means we need good telemetry so central knows when edges allowed local bursts. Otherwise reconciliation will look like a billing surprise.
quota-bot: INFO: smoothing-service v1.3 deployed to canary at 2026-02-18T08:12:23Z.
david: also need to decide how to expose this in Console: show current smoothing factor per-org and a timeline of edge-local burst admissions. Emma, UX thoughts?
emma: show a simple slider in advanced quotas: "burst forgiveness window" with tooltip. default = 30s. Advanced panel for observability: show per-org smoothing graph + top sources.
sara: must also add billing note: when we retro-apply credits after reconciliation, show an entry in invoice adjustments. Avoid surprise charges.
priya: another technical edge case: multi-key clients where keys share an org. If we enforce per-key strictly at edge, a client can open many keys to bypass org limits.
david: we should treat keys as identities but also have an org-level reconciler that caps aggregate usage. Enforcement order matters: edge enforces key-level soft limit, central enforces org-level hard limit.
maya: algorithm sketch for smoothing: keep EWMA of recent rps and max short-window peak. smoothing_alloc = clamp(EWMA + beta * (short_peak - EWMA), min=0.2, max=1.0). beta tuned to 0.5.
chris: can we add a noisy-neighbor detector based on cross-tenant sudden covariance? If many keys in one infra pool spike with similar profiles -> mark noisy.
sara: sounds good. That detector can trigger an automated temporary dampening policy against that tenant rather than reducing everyone's share.
david: one more operational thought: rollout strategy. We should A/B the new hybrid smoothing on 5% of orgs, observe errors and OOO complaints. Noisy-neighbor detector should be off for A/B to isolate effects.
emma: for Console, toggle should be opt-in initially and we default to off for orgs > enterprise (they get manual opt-in via success team).
priya: code/config snippet for the per-edge admission control I propose: 
```
# edge token bucket config
local_burst_tokens: 128
local_burst_window_s: 5
local_replenish_rate: org_rate / 1s
```
chris: keep local_burst_tokens conservative; 128 might be too high for small machines. Suggest 32 default.
maya: telemetry keys to track for canary: `smoothing_alloc`, `edge_admit_tokens`, `central_rejects`, `reconciliation_delta` (tokens).
quota-bot: METRIC: emitted smoothing_alloc for canary org 12345 = 0.45 at 2026-02-18T09:03:01Z
david: next steps: priya to prototype hybrid admission + reconciliation, maya to add metrics and dashboard applescript, emma to mock Console UX, sara to spec billing adjustment flow. Plan doc in #eng-platform by EOD.
priya: I can start a spike branch. Will post short RFC.
maya: i'll throw a quick Grafana panel in the canary dashboard under "QoS -> Smoothing".
emma: will do the mockups and show on Monday 10:30.
sara: I'll map possible invoice line items and a user-visible note.
david: great. if we can get spike data and an initial dashboard tomorrow we can decide whether to opt-in canary. :thumbsup:
